newsitem.title: NORWAY: Tanker moors up to Statfjord, oil output still cut.
newsitem.headline: Tanker moors up to Statfjord, oil output still cut.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Monday one shuttle tanker had moored up to the offshore loading buoy at the North Sea Statfjord B development, but weather conditions remained too difficult to begin oil loadings.
Two other vessels continued to wait at Statfjord for a break in weather conditions, which have prevented offshore crude loadings since Friday.
Two further ships were close by the Gullfaks field, Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said.

Statoil reduced output at Statfjord, Gullfaks and the Statfjord North and East satellites to a minimum due to burgeoning storage capacity. Throughput at the Snorre, Vigdis and Tordis developments was completely closed on Sunday.

"We have one ship hooked up at Statfjord B and we're waiting to seen if we can get the others in. We expect to start loadings later in early evening," Steihaug said. "As soon as we start loading we can start operations again to return to normal production."

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrel per day (bpd) and processes crude from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre and Vigdis developments, which in total add roughly 400,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
Gullfaks produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 85,000 bpd of output from the Tordis field.
